Likelihood Estimation (MLE) pre-training is a flexible approach to boost Neural Machine Translation (NMT), recent studies suggest these improvements mostly arise from promoting tokens that were already likely post-pre-training. We propose that the vast action space constitutes the primary impediment to RL success in machine translation. To validate this, we performed two series of experiments that are difficult to distinguish in typical RL settings. Firstly, keeping the action space constant while varying dataset sizes revealed outcomes tracking the inverse relationship between the dataset scale and the action space dimension. Secondly, with an extensive action space fixed, evaluating RL performance across different language groups showed improvement trends inversely correlated with the inverse degree. These findings remained consistent even when the vocabulary size was held constant but the sequence length was varied.
